blocks.passage:
Feedback is information. It helps us know what is working well, and what we can do better.

Good feedback is short, clear and kind. We say something positive, and then, if needed, we mention one thing to improve. We do not give a long list of problems — just one or two useful points.

Getting feedback is also a skill. Listen calmly, say thank you, and ask a question if you need to understand better. Do not defend yourself right away.

items.q: What is feedback, according to the text?
What is good feedback like?
items.why: "Good feedback is short, clear and kind."

items.q: How many things to improve should you mention?
How should you receive feedback?
options: Listen calmly, say thank you, and ask a question if needed
items.why: "Listen calmly, say thank you, and ask a question if you need to understand better."

items.q: What should you NOT do when getting feedback?

audio.text:
João just gave a good presentation, and I want to give him some quick feedback. Watch how I keep it short, clear and kind.

First, the positive. And I mean it — I don't just say 'good job'. 'João, that was really clear. The three main points were easy to follow, and you looked at the audience the whole time. Well done.'

Now, one thing to improve. Just one, not a list. 'One small idea for next time: at the end, you spoke a little fast. If you slow down on the last slide, the conclusion will land even better.'

See? One positive, said honestly. One improvement, said kindly. That's it. I don't bury him in ten problems — he'd remember none of them and just feel bad.

And notice I end on a good note: 'But honestly, that was a strong presentation. The client will be impressed.'

Good feedback helps someone grow and still feel good. Short, clear, kind — one thing to keep, one thing to try.

items.q: **Feedback** is…
options: information that helps you know what works and what to improve

items.q: To **improve** means to…
Choose the correct word: "That was a **___** point — it really helped."
Being **kind** means being…
Choose the correct word: "When you get feedback, stay **___**."
"**Well done** on the presentation!" Well done means…
"I'll end **on a good note**." To end on a good note means to…
items.why: On a good note = de forma positiva.

items.q: "Don't **take it personally**." To take something personally means to…
options: feel hurt as if it's an attack on you
items.why: Take personally = levar para o lado pessoal.

items.q: "One thing to **work on** next time." To work on something means to…
"Thanks, I'll **keep that in mind**." To keep something in mind means to…
items.why: Keep in mind = ter em mente.
